title: The terminal drawer is mounted only while the thread runtime's isTerminalVisible is true, and enters and leaves on a bottom-edge move combined with a fade
source_evidence: DroppyCode/App/Views/Chat/ChatView.swift:280-283 - if runtime.isTerminalVisible { TerminalPanel(runtime: runtime, directory: directory).transition(.move(edge: .bottom).combined(with: .opacity)) }
DroppyCode/App/Views/Chat/ChatView.swift:294 - .animation(switching ? nil : Chrome.panelSlide, value: runtime.isTerminalVisible)
DroppyCode/App/Views/Chat/ChatView.swift:95 - let switching = sceneThreadID != runtime.threadID
porting/extracts/chrome-design-tokens.md:347 - Chrome.panelSlide is .spring(response: 0.32, dampingFraction: 0.9), or .easeOut(duration: 0.18) under Reduce Motion
preconditions: A thread is selected and its chat column is on screen.
action: runtime.isTerminalVisible becomes true or false.
expected_result: The panel is inserted below the composer inside the chat column's VStack(spacing: 0) and animates in by moving up from the bottom edge while fading in; hiding reverses it. The animation is Chrome.panelSlide, which is .spring(response: 0.32, dampingFraction: 0.9) normally and .easeOut(duration: 0.18) when the system reports Reduce Motion. While the chat column is still showing a thread other than the scene's thread (switching), the animation is nil, so the change is applied with no motion at all.
side_effects: Mounting the panel runs its .onAppear, which calls terminals.ensureTerminal and can spawn a shell process (see PR-TERM-004).
persistence: isTerminalVisible is per-thread runtime state and is not persisted; it is false for every new runtime (ThreadRuntime.swift:239).
failure_cases: No thread selected: the chat column is not rendered at all, so the panel cannot appear.
windows_path: Renderer-side conditional mount with the same spring and ease pair, reading the OS Reduce Motion preference (SPI_GETCLIENTAREAANIMATION on Windows). Platform boundary: the Reduce Motion source.
verification_method: interaction test asserting mount and unmount, plus capture comparison of the transition

windows_path: pointerup; write the same key with the same name and type.
verification_method: restart test: drag, quit, relaunch, assert the height

source_evidence: DroppyCode/App/Views/Terminal/TerminalPanel.swift:306 - .help(session.isRunning ? session.title : session.title + " \u00b7 the shell has exited")

DroppyCode/App/Views/Terminal/TerminalPanel.swift:307-309 - .accessibilityElement(children: .contain), .accessibilityLabel(Text(session.isRunning ? session.title : session.title + ", the shell has exited")), .accessibilityAddTraits(isSelected ? [.isButton, .isSelected] : .isButton)
preconditions: A session exists, running or exited.
action: The user hovers the tab, or a screen reader reads it.
expected_result: Running: tooltip and accessibility label are both exactly the session title. Exited: the tooltip is the title, a space, U+00B7 MIDDLE DOT, a space, then "the shell has exited"; the accessibility label is the title, a comma, a space, then "the shell has exited". The two strings differ deliberately and must not be unified. The tab is an accessibility container with the button trait, plus the selected trait when it is the selected tab.
windows_path: Same two strings byte for byte, including U+00B7. UI Automation: ControlType Button, SelectionItemPattern IsSelected for the selected tab, Name set to the accessibility variant.
verification_method: unit test on the string builders plus an accessibility-tree assertion
